title: A Postcard for the Tide
premise: Sebastian Okafor, a wedding planner who walked away from their own engagement twelve years ago, has built a careful life arranging other people's perfect days. When a water-damaged postcard surfaces — written by Sebastian eleven years ago, never sent, addressed to the person they abandoned, marine biologist Wren Halloway — it arrives with news that Wren is dying and has spent years searching for the sender. To reach Wren before time runs out, Sebastian must dismantle the safe life they built, confront the injustice that drove them apart (Wren was framed for research fraud by the institute Sebastian's family protected), and finally speak the sentence rehearsed for a decade: the truth of why they left. In the end, love does not arrive as rescue but as witness — Sebastian reaches Wren in time not to save them from dying, but to give them back their name, their cleared record, and one true wedding on the shore where it all began.
about_author: Astrid Kavanagh is a former coastal archivist who spent years cataloguing undelivered mail washed ashore in Cornwall, an experience that haunts every page she writes. She lives above a shuttered post office with her partner and a dog named Postmark.

chapters.title: The Weight of White Peonies
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. A flawless society wedding collapses when the bride confesses cold feet; Sebastian talks her down with practiced ease while feeling nothing. Establishes their meticulous craft and private numbness. Emotional beat: competence as armor.

chapters.title: Twelve Years of Small Steps
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. A quiet morning routine reveals the architecture of safety: no contracts over six months, no second dates past three, a locked drawer they never open. Flashback flicker of a ring returned. Beat: the cost of caution.

chapters.title: What the Tide Brought In
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Cleaning out their late mother's seaside cottage, Sebastian finds a water-stained postcard in her belongings — their own handwriting, dated eleven years ago, addressed to Wren Halloway, never sent. Beat: the past breaches the seawall.

chapters.title: The Sentence I Never Sent
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Reading the postcard's few lines — 'I should have stayed. I should have told them everything' — Sebastian remembers writing it drunk on a ferry and losing it overboard. Or believing they did. Beat: vertigo of a choice made long ago.

chapters.title: A Name in the News
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Searching Wren's name, Sebastian finds a fundraising page: Wren Halloway, celebrated marine biologist, terminally ill, still asking one question publicly — who wrote the anonymous letter that once saved her career? Beat: hope with a deadline attached.

chapters.title: The Client Who Wasn't
chapters.summary: Wren's POV, eleven years earlier. A young researcher watches her fraud trial collapse because an anonymous document arrived at the ethics board. She keeps the envelope. Beat: gratitude aimed at a ghost.

chapters.title: The Family Business
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Dinner with brother Marcus, now general counsel at the Ashcombe Institute, reveals the family still guards the old secret: Professor Aldous Vane falsified data, and Wren took the fall until someone intervened. Beat: duty versus truth, the original wound.

chapters.title: Booking the Impossible Wedding
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. A new client requests a wedding on the Cornish coast — miles from Wren's hospice town. Sebastian takes it, telling themselves it's coincidence. Beat: self-deception dressed as professionalism.

chapters.title: Postmark Eleven Years Late
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. In the hospice garden, Wren rereads the anonymous exoneration letter and tells her sister Nell she wants, before dying, to thank its author. Nell hires a tracing agent. Beat: two searches converging.

chapters.title: The Drawer Opens
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Sebastian unlocks the drawer kept shut for twelve years: photographs, the returned ring, and a duplicate of the postcard's draft. They book a train ticket, then cancel it. Then rebook it. Beat: courage in increments.

chapters.title: Marcus Warns Me Off
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Marcus learns of the trip and pleads: reopening the Vane affair exposes the Institute, their mother's legacy, Sebastian's career. 'Some verdicts are better left wrong.' Beat: the family debt made explicit.

chapters.title: The Coast Road
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Driving west, Sebastian rehearses the sentence — 'I'm the one who wrote it' — at every service station, unable to finish it aloud. Beat: rehearsal without release.

chapters.title: Tidepool Lessons
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren teaches a hospice volunteer to read tidepools, deflecting questions about regret. Privately she admits the unfinished search hurts more than the diagnosis. Beat: grace over grief.

chapters.title: The Wrong Door
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Arriving in Porthmere, Sebastian goes to Wren's old address and finds strangers. A neighbor mentions the hospice on the headland — and that visitors must be approved family. Beat: proximity without permission.

chapters.title: Nell at the Gate
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Wren's sister Nell blocks the hospice door: Wren doesn't need pitying exes in her last months. Sebastian, unable to explain the postcard or the letter, retreats. Beat: justice delayed reads as abandonment.

chapters.title: A Wedding on the Headland
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Surveying the client's venue — a clifftop hotel overlooking the hospice — Sebastian realizes the geography of their escape route and their destination are the same. Beat: fate disguised as logistics.

chapters.title: What Vane Took
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren dictates a memoir chapter about the scandal: how Aldous Vane destroyed her data, how the Institute closed ranks, how an anonymous letter turned the board overnight. Beat: the record she refuses to let die.

chapters.title: The Archive Box
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. In the cottage attic, Sebastian finds their mother's correspondence: letters showing she knew the truth, helped suppress it, and later anonymously funded Wren's reinstated fellowship — guilt paid in installments. Beat: inheritance of complicity.

chapters.title: Two Truths, One Letter
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Sebastian understands now: their mother intercepted the postcard years ago, and the anonymous exoneration letter may have been assembled from Sebastian's own evidence, mailed by her. The rescue was theirs; the silence was too. Beat: grief reframed as legacy.

chapters.title: Storm Warning
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. A seizure lands Wren in the hospice ward. Nell, frightened, calls the tracing agent to hurry. Wren dreams of the sea giving something back. Beat: the clock audibly ticking.

chapters.title: The Client Confession
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. The bride-to-be, sensing Sebastian's distraction, asks what they're running from. Sebastian tells a stranger the whole story for the first time — and hears, aloud, how cowardly the silence sounds. Beat: confession as rehearsal.

chapters.title: Nell Finds the Postcard
chapters.summary: Nell's POV. Going through Wren's keepsakes, Nell discovers a photograph of Sebastian and a matchbook from the ferry bar, and connects the dots. She confronts Sebastian at the hotel: 'You're the ghost she's been thanking.' Beat: exposure.

chapters.title: Denied
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Nell gives Sebastian one hour with Wren — then rescinds it after learning Sebastian's family helped bury the truth. 'You don't get absolution on a schedule.' Beat: the door closing on earned forgiveness.

chapters.title: The Institute's Offer
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Marcus arrives with a deal: the Institute will quietly clear Wren's record if everyone signs an NDA and the Vane file stays sealed. Justice as transaction. Beat: the theme sharpened — law without justice.

chapters.title: What Wren Wants
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Told of the offer, Wren refuses: 'I don't want my name laundered. I want it said out loud, where it counts.' She asks Nell to find the letter's author herself. Beat: dignity over remedy.

chapters.title: The Rehearsal Dinner
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Running the client's rehearsal dinner flawlessly while hollow, Sebastian watches two families toast lies of omission and recognizes their own reflection. That night they write the sentence down and sign it. Beat: the armor cracks.

chapters.title: Breaking the Seal
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Sebastian sends the Institute a copy of their mother's letters and their own sworn statement naming Vane, forfeiting the family settlement and their professional references. Marcus calls it betrayal; Sebastian calls it mail, finally delivered. Beat: the point of no return.

chapters.title: Vane Answers
chapters.summary: Antagonist POV. Elderly Aldous Vane, alerted by the filing, visits Sebastian with velvet threats: reputations are fragile things, and funerals forgive everyone. Sebastian holds ground for the first time in twelve years. Beat: fear met with spine.

chapters.title: The Storm Makes the Decision
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. A storm floods the coast road; the wedding relocates inland, stranding Sebastian in Porthmere. With roads closed and excuses gone, Sebastian walks to the hospice in the rain. Beat: circumstance stripping away the last alibi.

chapters.title: The Sentence
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. At Wren's bedside, Sebastian finally says it: 'I wrote the letter. My mother mailed it. And I left because staying meant testifying against my family — and I chose them. Choosing you now, late, is all I have.' Wren laughs, then weeps. Beat: climax of truth-telling.

chapters.title: Not Forgiveness Yet
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren doesn't absolve Sebastian — 'You don't get the ending you rehearsed' — but asks them to stay, as witness, not lover. Days of tidepool talk and memoir dictation follow. Beat: love rebuilt on honesty, not nostalgia.

chapters.title: The Board Sits Again
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. The Institute, exposed, reconvenes; Vane's fraud is formally acknowledged and Wren's record restored publicly. Marcus resigns rather than defend the indefensible — then, quietly, leaves the door ajar. Beat: justice outside the law, won anyway.

chapters.title: A Proposal, Improvised
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Clear-headed on a good day, Wren asks Sebastian not for forever but for one true wedding — the thing Sebastian plans but no longer believes in. 'Plan me one honest day.' Beat: the genre's promise, inverted.

chapters.title: Planning Against Time
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Sebastian pours twelve years of withheld belief into one week: vows, wildflowers, a borrowed boat, guests drawn from both broken families. Marcus agrees to walk Wren's wheelchair down the aisle. Beat: craft becomes devotion.

chapters.title: Vane at the Edge of the Guest List
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Vane sends a lawyer to contest the public statement; Sebastian chooses to invite him instead — 'Come watch what your silence built.' He doesn't come, but the threat dissolves. Beat: power surrendered by refusing the fight.

chapters.title: The Wedding on the Shore
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV. On the headland at low tide, Wren and Sebastian exchange vows written on the back of the unsent postcard. Nell reads the eleven-year-old words aloud. The sea takes a petal; nobody minds. Beat: emotional peak — love against duty, duty renounced.

chapters.title: Nine Days
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Nine good days after the wedding: dawn swims in the shallows, dictated final chapters, an argument about peonies versus sea thrift that ends in laughter. Beat: sweetness without denial.

chapters.title: What the Tide Takes
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Wren dies at dawn with Sebastian's hand in hers, the postcard tucked under her pillow. Grief arrives not as collapse but as a tide going out — vast, quiet, survivable. Beat: the cost honored.

chapters.title: The Archive of Small Steps
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Months later, Sebastian reopens the business with new rules: no NDAs, ceremonies that tell the truth, a scholarship in Wren's name funded by the Institute's settlement. Marcus visits; some bridges hold. Beat: identity rebuilt.

chapters.title: A Postcard for the Tide
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV, coda. On the first anniversary, Sebastian writes a new postcard — 'I stayed' — and lets the sea take it from the same ferry rail. Walking back up the hill toward a couple waiting to be married, Sebastian believes again. Beat: resolution — love as practice, not protection.
